resolutions.title: The shared validator accepts malformed flag values that the captured CLI rejects
resolutions.action: Reproduced both cases before fixing (--web=garbage -> ok:true; --limit=garbage -> ok:true). The capture script now classifies each flag VALUE TYPE from the help line TYPE token (classifyType: int/number -> int, other -> string, absent -> boolean) and records it as value_type; the validator new checkValue reproduces the real CLI parse errors verbatim (invalid argument "garbage" for "-w, --web" flag: strconv.ParseBool ... and the ParseInt equivalent) for explicit =value forms and consumed values alike, while reference placeholders (<url>, <owner>/<repo>) stay exempt. The contract was re-captured against gh 2.91.0; --limit now records {long:--limit, short:-L, takes_value:true, value_type:int}. Both reproductions are negative fixtures in the sweep; --limit=5 still passes.

resolutions.title: Schema extraction silently drops documented fields based on formatting
resolutions.action: Replaced the two-space regex with topLevelKeys, a STRUCTURAL brace/bracket-depth walk that skips string contents, so a second key on the same line and a four-space-indented key are both found; the field-note extractor now collects EVERY backticked subject in a bolded bullet run, so restoring the grouped categories_run / categories_skipped bullet no longer hides a subject. Both of the reviewer mutations ship as negative fixtures (formatting cannot hide a documented key; a grouped field-note bullet contributes EVERY subject it names).

resolutions.title: Unknown command families bypass the snippet sweep entirely
resolutions.action: The extractor is now family-free: ghSnippets matches gh <token> ... by SHAPE and lets the contract lookup reject unsupported commands, so gh frobnicate --repo <owner>/<repo> is caught and rejected as an unknown command (a negative fixture). Copyable-vs-prose is decided by a family-free rule (the snippet carries at least one flag), since every real invocation in these references is repository-qualified and therefore flagged; that rule replaced the accidental filtering the old repo|pr regex did, which shape extraction exposed by catching prose mentions like gh pr create erroring. Every negative fixture now runs THROUGH the extractor rather than being handed to snippetArgv directly.

final_assessment: 7 of 7 resolved; 0 unresolved markers in scope. The three CRITICALs were one mistake at three layers — an instrument built to end remembered truths was itself built on remembered structure: remembered formatting (a two-space key regex), remembered command families (a repo|pr prefix), and remembered flag names without their captured types. All three now derive from structure or from the contract: brace-depth key extraction, shape-based snippet extraction with contract lookup deciding legality, and recorded value_type per flag with the real CLI parse errors reproduced. The decision-lane finding was ratified as option B: the audit-drift reference is reverted to its documented shape and its three-way contradiction with two archived requirements is a dated, EXACT, pinned follow-up owned by rc07 rather than a correction this stage may make past its size ceiling — my own in-context pass had wrongly declared baseline compliance after checking one capability. Quote-aware tokenizing makes the two consumers agree on quoted values; module-relative paths fix the explicit-root run (reproduced both ways); the artifacts state their inventory from the diff. 2036 -> 2040 tests green across 93 files; the suite passes with no host gh on PATH; strict-valid; the surface refresh changed exactly the two references touched.
